item.title: Play
item.description: A 16-bit hockey game for the players and families of our association. Pick your team and your age level: the rink, the number of players, the rules and the parents in the stands all change with it. New here? Read how to play , then see why the rink changes with age .

item.title: Age levels and the ADM
item.description: The game follows the idea behind USA Hockey's American Development Model (ADM) : kids play on a surface and with a team size that fits them. Smaller ice and fewer players mean more puck touches, more shots, more decisions and more fun. item.title: Penalties
item.description: Every penalty in the game comes from the USA Hockey rulebook. When the ref calls one, the game stops for a moment to show the ref's signal and explain the rule. item.title: Behind the game
item.description: This is a game first. It's also a way to show why the ADM recommendations matter, and to poke at the darker side of youth sports: money, influence and exposure, as opposed to kids just having a great time. The stands Every kid on the ice has their own section of fans, from one to eight. When a kid does something good, their super fans go wild, jumping far higher than anyone around them. item.title: For families
item.description: The thing that helps your kid the most is also the easiest: relax, enjoy watching them, and support them. Cheer for effort, win or lose. Let the coaches coach and the refs ref. item.title: The teams
item.description: Four teams, each with home and away kits. All the rosters are made up: invented names and invented numbers. AAAA Sparkle Selects : neon pink, with yellow and blue. B Squad : black and pink. Saber Cats : black and electric green. Icers : navy and white. Every team carries 13 skaters and 2 goalies. Each player has ratings for skating, shooting, passing, stickhandling, checking and stamina, plus coachability and exposure. You can read how those last two work in behind the game .
